evidence_context: The tutor's language model uses a decoder-only transformer to process text. A tokenizer divides an input passage into tokens, and an embedding layer maps those tokens to numerical vectors. Positional information helps the transformer distinguish sequences containing the same tokens in different orders. In each attention layer, self-attention combines information from token representations. A causal attention mask prevents a position from attending to later positions when the model predicts the next token. This restriction applies during both training and generation. Attention can connect information across a passage, but the model's finite context window limits the amount of text available in a single request. An attention weight does not establish that the associated claim is true.

evidence_context: Evaluation must distinguish the quality of retrieval from the quality of the generated answer. Retrieval recall measures how many relevant passages the search returns, while retrieval precision measures how many returned passages are relevant. Neither measure alone shows whether the tutor uses the retrieved evidence correctly. An answer can cite a real passage while making a claim that the passage does not support. The tutor is therefore evaluated for factual correctness, support from the supplied documents, and appropriate handling of uncertainty. When two course passages disagree, the tutor should identify the disagreement rather than combine them into an unsupported conclusion. A failure to retrieve supporting evidence means that support was not found; it does not prove that the proposed claim is false.
